note: Alexander of Macedon put ten questions to the Elders of the Negev: about distances, the order of creation (they declined to say whether light or darkness came first), who is wise, mighty and rich, how to live and how to die. When they said that even Satan is sometimes victorious, he threatened to execute them; they replied that falsehood does not suit a king, and he dressed them in purple and gold chains. Using their advice to cross the Mountains of Darkness, he reached a town of women, who served him bread of gold, and he wrote on its gate that he had learned sense from women. At a spring he guessed it flowed from the Garden of Eden. One version says he reached its gate, was refused, and was given an eyeball that outweighed all his gold, until it was covered with dust.
why: The Gemara has been explaining where the daily offerings were slaughtered by the position of the sun; Alexander's first question, answered from how hard it is to look at the sun at midday, ties the story to that discussion.
